subject.title: ACP: support non-thread persistent affinity for cron and orchestrator sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class ACP persistent-affinity `sessions_spawn` contract for cron, hook, and orchestrator callers, and what ownership/lifecycle scope should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent contract controls who can reuse a persistent ACP harness session and how that session is cleaned up or preserved across failed dispatches.

options.title: Adopt scoped ACP affinity
options.body: Add a narrow `mode="persistent"` plus `affinityKey`-style contract restricted to cron/hook/orchestrator owners and scoped by requester identity, backend, cwd, and affinity key.

options.title: Fold into broader non-thread sessions
options.body: Resolve this under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/53548 if maintainers want one general non-thread persistent-session contract instead of a cron/hook-specific ACP path.

options.title: Decline core affinity
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core thread-bound for persistent ACP and route optional orchestration experiments to plugins unless a missing core API is identified.

recommendation.title: Adopt scoped ACP affinity
recommendation.body: Add a narrow `mode="persistent"` plus `affinityKey`-style contract restricted to cron/hook/orchestrator owners and scoped by requester identity, backend, cwd, and affinity key.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACP spawn and cron-adjacent refactors make this the strongest available routing candidate for the product/security boundary decision.
